explanation: Mixture of formatting/boilerplate positions: strongest on the decade digit in copyright years ('Copyright (c) 20[1]x'), plus figure-reference tokens ('Fig', 'FIG.', '0[.]3\textwidth'), the '[' opening a paper body after a YAML front-matter '---', zip-code digits and image filename extensions. Ordinary prose tokens are weak.

Fires on tokens inside programming code or technical Q&A text, especially language keywords and line-initial words (struct, class, function, with, extends, UPDATE, 'go test', YAML keys like 'address'), and on words of a developer's prose question adjacent to code. Weak or silent in non-technical prose.

Fires on structural/syntactic tokens in code, documentation markup and metadata headers: '@param', '\usage', '\item', YAML 'title:' / bibliography '-' list items, 'struct {', 'do', ':' after class names, newline after 'package x', plus legal case captions ',v.' and subtitle timestamps. Natural prose is weak.

Fires mid-sentence in natural prose on loosely related spots: the tail of an acronym defined in parentheses ('(CR[RT])', '(ES[RD])', '(MD[R])'), weight-class and ranking words ('flyweight', 'division', 'fourth', 'second round'), and words inside set phrases ('a pound of', 'in part', 'half-full'). No clear single trigger.

Fires on a word-internal continuation subtoken that completes a word split into several tokens, especially rare or technical words (Water[gate], subd[ural], immunoh[isto]chemistry, micro[grams], s[ipped], culpr[its], at[ax]ia), in any language. Whole-word tokens and code are weak.

Mixture: adverbs/modifiers in prose ('really', 'always', 'recently', 'equally', 'respectfully', 'prelim[inarily]'), path components in imports ('k8s.io[/apimachinery]', 'management[/__]init__'), Japanese text tokens and some proper nouns ('Safari', 'bullpen', 'capital'). No shared feature.

Fires on assorted tokens in ordinary English prose: final digits of years ('199[6]', '200[2]'), prepositions ending phrases ('fitting [in]', 'in accounting [for]', 'appeared this week [in]'), and nouns completing short phrases ('the [mirror]', 'a [wife]', 'take [pictures]'). No clear unifying trigger.

Two main triggers: 'of' after 'free' (especially 'Permission is hereby granted, free [of] charge' in licenses; also 'free of fillers') and CamelCase class/identifier pieces in code, especially Android imports ('android.view[.LayoutInflater]', '.AsyncTask', 'setMinimumTrack[TintColor]', 'Css[Lexer]'). Plus scattered name/acronym fragments.

Fires on the first token or two of a document's opening sentence, right after a title, heading or 'Q:' line (e.g. 'I[ have]' after a Stack Exchange question title, 'Say', 'Okay', 'The', 'A:'). Same tokens later in a document are weak.

Fires on subword pieces containing 'l' clusters like 'yl', 'il', 'el', 'll', 'yll' inside words, strongest in chemical names (sial[yl], sial[yll]actose, polys[il]icon, my[el]operoxidase, diacy[lg]lycerol) and also names (S[yl]veon, Sie[gel], Hy[ll]as, Se[ville]). Code and function words are weak.

Fires on the word that completes a highly predictable fixed phrase or idiom in prose ('feel [free]', 'Of [course]', 'second most [common]', 'at [first]', 'as [published]', 'names [of] its contributors', 'NONPRECED[ENTIAL]', 'First of [all]'). Less predictable tokens are weak.

Mixture with no evident theme: place-name pieces in addresses ('Overland [Park]', 'Urb[ana]'), digits in citations and code, config constant parts ('COM_POST[INSTALL]'), class-name pieces ('ChildProcess[Reporter]'), and function words in prose ('the', 'a', 'also').

Fires on names of software developer tools and IDEs, and on tool-usage contexts: 'IntelliJ [IDEA]', '[git] branch', 'TortoiseSV[N]', 'Grad[le]', 'swagger', 'Auto[CAD]', 'gitlab', plus 'used [for]/[to]' after a tool or instrument name. General prose is weak.

Mixture: 'you' in GPL/LGPL boilerplate ('This program is free software;[ you] can redistribute'), domain suffixes in URLs ('.org', '.net'), and word-final suffix pieces completing words ('Multithread[ed]', 'determin[ing]', 'Depart[ments]', 'Cavend[ish]'), plus non-English tokens.

Fires on varied tokens with no evident theme: Portuguese/French verbs and prepositions ('tent[ar]', 'estar', 'pela', 'été'), punctuation in URLs/versions/code ('https[://]', '4.0[.]', 'version[="]', 'from __future__[ import]'), and prose function words.

Fires on 'This' starting a sentence, strongest at the start of a code file header comment ('/*\n * [This] file is part of', '// This code was generated') and abstract openings ('abstract: [This] paper'); moderately on sentence-initial 'This' in prose and on 'this/these' as determiners mid-sentence; weak otherwise.

Fires on words that locate or refer to a part/position, such as 'the [following]', 'the [above]', 'on the [other] hand', 'Western region', 'Northeast', and CJK equivalents (部 'part', 下列 'following', どの 'which', 第 ordinal). Most strongly in Chinese/Japanese text.

Mostly fires on the first element of technical compound terms in physics/science ('[quantum] dot', 'cavity[-Q]ED', '[time]-of-flight', '[multi]dimensional', 'Q-system'), with 'quantum' the most common trigger; also on medical prefix pieces ('bip[olar]', 'hem[ip]aresis', 'null[ip]arous') and some name fragments.

Fires on pieces of Japanese personal and place names in romaji or kanji (Kamikita 'K'oi, 木[村], Kigata [D]oman, Is[sei], Momoyama [G]akuin) and on the number slot after 'Japanese Patent ... No.'. Strongest within Japanese-name contexts; non-Japanese text is weak.

Fires on syntax punctuation and operators in imperative code statements, especially inside for-loop headers and if conditions: ';' in 'for (i = 0; i < n;', '=' in assignments, ')' and ' {' closing conditions, '&&', '+', 'return'. Prose and declarations are weak.

Fires on tokens at or near the end of the first sentence or clause of a document (the first '?', '.', or the next word such as 'And', 'Will', 'It', 'which'), i.e. early-document sentence-boundary positions. The same tokens deep into a document are weak.
